transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, because it's probably just a small thing, really. But... well, I guess what made me come in is that I’ve been having a little trouble at work lately. 

I'm a receptionist, and I've started sort of... losing my place while I’m scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays. It's not that I can't do my job! I always get it done. It's just that my mind kind of slips off track sometimes, mostly because I get so busy thinking about little things I might have overlooked. 

Does that make sense as a reason to be here? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out.
Can you describe what kinds of thoughts tend to distract you when you're at work? Are they specific worries or ideas that keep coming back, even if you try to focus on something else?

Well, it's mostly just... silly little things, really. Nothing major! Just things like, did I remember to log that cancellation properly, or did I order the right printer toner? 

I know I did, and I try to just tell myself, 'Sunny, it's handled.' But... I don't know, the thought just kind of keeps looping? And then, before I know it, I've gone from that one little concern to another, and another, until I'm just checking all these tiny details in my head over and over again. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably makes me sound a bit scattered or disorganized. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or mental steps—like checking, organizing, or thinking specific thoughts—to try to feel more certain or to reduce anxiety?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I do anything like that. I mean, I always double-check my work, of course, because I want to be thorough for the clinic and the patients! But just the normal amount, really. 

I don't have, like, a special routine or anything where I have to organize my desk a certain way or keep checking things physically over and over to feel okay. It's really just... the thoughts kind of lingering in my head, like I mentioned before. I definitely don't do anything too unusual or disruptive! 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not misunderstanding the question.
Are these looping thoughts something you find upsetting or intrusive, or do they feel more like just a normal part of thinking through your tasks?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't call them upsetting! Intrusive sounds so... serious, you know? I definitely don't want to give you the wrong idea. 

I think it really just feels like a normal part of thinking through my tasks, exactly like you said. It's just my brain trying to be extra careful because I really want to do a good job for the clinic. Maybe it gets a tiny bit annoying sometimes when I'm trying to move on to the next thing, but it's nothing bad. 

It's completely normal to want to be thorough like that, right? I just hope I'm explaining it okay and not making a big deal out of nothing.
Do these thoughts ever cause you significant stress or make it hard for you to complete your work on time?

Oh, well... I definitely wouldn't say they cause significant stress! I mean, I'm still showing up every day and getting through all my tasks. I'd hate to be a burden on the clinic. 

I guess... well, maybe scheduling takes me just a little bit longer now? Only because I double-check myself so much to make sure I don't double-book anyone. And, um, there was this one time I had to redo parts of the lobby displays because I kind of lost track of what I was arranging... 

But really, I still get everything done! It just might take a tiny bit more effort sometimes. That doesn't sound too bad, does it? I just want to make sure I'm still doing a good job.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even outside of work?

Oh, no, no, definitely not! I haven't been feeling sad or down at all. I mean, I still really enjoy my life and my job. 

I still like doing the things I always do outside of work... like spending time with my family and keeping the house nice. I don't feel depressed or anything like that, I promise. I'm generally a very positive person! 

I just... well, maybe I'm just a little tired sometimes from, you know, making sure everything is done right at the clinic. But that's totally normal for a working mom, right? I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm unhappy, because I'm truly not!
Do you ever have thoughts that pop up in your mind that you don’t want or that bother you, even if they’re about small things?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Not at all! Like... bad or weird thoughts? No, definitely not. 

My mind is pretty much just focused on, you know, my daily tasks and taking care of my family. I don't have things popping up that I don't want there. I mean, just the normal reminders to double-check the clinic schedule or pick up groceries, but nothing that actually bothers me or feels out of place. 

That's a good sign, right? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way and giving you what you need.
Have you ever had the experience of thoughts that didn’t feel like your own, or that someone else was putting thoughts into your mind?

Oh, my goodness, no! No, never anything like that. That sounds really scary, honestly. 

My thoughts are definitely my own. I mean, they might be a little busy sometimes, just with all the things I need to remember for the clinic and the kids, but they're always mine. No one is putting anything in my head, I promise. 

I'm completely normal in that way! I hope that's the right answer... I just wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I'm very grounded!
Do you ever feel the need to repeat certain thoughts or actions in your mind or in real life to try to prevent something bad from happening or to make things feel 'just right'?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I like things to be organized at the front desk, of course, because that's just part of being a good receptionist. But I don't ever feel like I have to repeat things or do them over and over to stop something bad from happening. 

I just do my tasks once, you know, maybe double-check my work like anyone else would, and then move on to the next thing. I don't have any rituals or anything like that. That's a good thing, right? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information. I really don't have any habits like that, I promise!
Are there certain thoughts that keep coming back, even if you don’t want them, and do they make you feel anxious even if you try not to act on them?

Well... I mean, I guess sometimes I do get stuck on things a little bit. But not in a weird way! Just... normal worrying, you know? Like, I'll tell myself, "Sunny, it’s handled, you took care of it," but the thought just kind of... keeps looping around in my head anyway. 

And then, before I know it, I've gone from worrying about that one little thing to worrying about another thing, and another, until I’m just... checking all the details in my head over and over again to make sure everything is okay. It does make me a little anxious, but I don't act on it or do anything strange! I just think about it a lot. 

Is that what you mean? I hope that makes sense. It's really just because I care so much about doing a good job and making sure my family is okay. That's pretty normal, right?
Even if you don't act on these thoughts or feel overly upset, do they ever cause you enough distraction or discomfort that it interferes with how efficiently you can work or function during the day?

Well, I mean... I wouldn't say it interferes too much. I'm definitely still showing up every day and getting through everything I need to do! I pride myself on being reliable. 

I guess... maybe... scheduling appointments takes me just a tiny bit longer now? Only because I want to be absolutely sure I didn't make a mistake, so I might double-check things a little more than I used to. And, well, there was this one time recently where I was putting together the informational displays in the lobby, and I got so wrapped up in my head that I kind of lost track of what I was doing and had to redo a section. 

But it's nothing major, I promise! I still get it all done, and the lobby always looks nice in the end. It's just me trying to be thorough. That's not too bad, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing things right.
Do you ever find it hard to stop thinking about something, even when you know it’s not important or when it gets in the way of doing other things?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean... if something really isn't important, I don't dwell on it. The things that do kind of get stuck in my head are always the important things, you know? Like making sure the front desk schedule is right for the next day, or just... hoping my family is safe and doing well. 

I wouldn't say I get hung up on silly or meaningless things at all. And I definitely don't let it stop me from doing what I need to do! Like I said, I'm always very careful to keep up with my work and my responsibilities. If something truly doesn't matter, I can just let it go and move on. 

That's a healthy way to handle it, right? I'm really trying to be as helpful as I can with all your questions, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Can you think of a time when one of these looping thoughts came up that you really wished would go away, but just kept coming back no matter how hard you tried to ignore it or push it out of your mind?

Well, I mean... I guess I sort of mentioned this earlier, but it's really just the normal stuff. Like, I'll tell myself, "Sunny, it’s handled, you took care of it," you know? I try to just push it away because I know I already dealt with it. 

But sometimes... the thought just keeps looping around anyway. And then, before I know it, I’ve gone from that one little concern to another one, and then another, until I’m just... checking all the details in my head over and over again to make sure everything is perfectly fine. 

I do wish I could just turn it off sometimes, but it's just because I want to be responsible! It's not like I'm obsessing over anything bad or weird. It's just me trying to be a good employee and a good mom. That's a completely normal way to feel, isn't it? I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to.

Even if you don’t consider them upsetting, do these looping thoughts ever cause you enough frustration or distraction that it affects your ability to focus on other things, like spending time with your family or relaxing after work?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it affects my family time! I'm very present with my kids, I always make sure of that. I mean, sure, sometimes when we're watching a movie or having dinner, my mind might drift for just a second to... oh, I don't know, whether I sent that one email or if the boys have everything they need for school the next day. 

But it's just a fleeting thought, really! It doesn't stop me from enjoying my time with them or relaxing. I just quickly run through my mental checklist, and then I'm right back in the moment. It's just a mom thing, you know? Always multitasking in your head. 

I definitely don't let it ruin my evenings or make me a distracted parent. I'm doing a good job balancing it all, I think. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how things are.

Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you really don’t want there, even if they’re not about anything dangerous or strange—like a word, image, or idea that keeps popping up and bothers you even a little?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, unless you count getting a silly commercial jingle stuck in your head from the radio on the way to work, but everybody gets that, right? 

I definitely don't have random words or images popping up that bother me or make me uncomfortable. I try to keep my mind pretty focused and, you know, positive. If something isn't helpful, I just don't dwell on it. So, no, nothing like that at all. 

I hope that's okay! I just want to make sure I'm understanding what you're asking and giving you the right information. Am I answering these the way you need me to?
Can you think of a time when a thought came into your mind that you really didn’t want there—something that surprised or unsettled you, even just a little—even if it wasn’t dangerous or strange?

Um... I'm really trying to think, because I want to give you a good answer, but... no, honestly. I know you just asked something kind of similar, and I really don't mean to be unhelpful! It's just that my thoughts are usually very... practical. 

You know, they're just focused on the schedule at the front desk, or what the kids need for dinner. I don't really have anything pop up that surprises me or makes me feel unsettled. I like to keep things pretty organized and normal in my head, so... yeah, I haven't noticed anything like that. 

Is it alright that I don't have an example for you? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need.

Even if they don’t bother you much, do you ever have thoughts that suddenly pop into your mind that you don’t want there—like a word, phrase, or idea—that you can’t seem to get rid of, even for a little while?

Oh, gosh. I feel like I'm giving you the same answer again, and I really hope that's not frustrating for you! But... no, I really don't. 

I don't have words or phrases that get stuck like that, where I can't get rid of them. My mind is just... well, it's very busy with all the normal things I have to do. The schedule, the kids, the house. But it's all stuff I *want* to be thinking about, you know? Because I need to stay on top of it all to be a good mom and do my job well at the clinic. 

So, no, nothing unwanted that I can't shake off. I really hope it's okay that I keep saying no to this! I just want to be completely honest with you so you can do your job. Am I still helping?
Even if they don’t bother you a lot, do these looping thoughts ever make you feel even a little bit frustrated, tense, or upset inside—like a nagging feeling you can’t quite shake?

I feel so bad, I really do, because I know you're trying to get to something specific, but... I don't really have looping thoughts to begin with. 

I mean, I definitely feel tense and frustrated sometimes! Oh, absolutely. But that's just... normal stress, right? Like when the phones won't stop ringing and I'm worried about getting my youngest to soccer practice on time. That makes me feel a little wound up, but it's not from a thought that's stuck on a loop. It's just from trying to keep everything running smoothly. 

I really don't have those nagging, unwanted thoughts you're describing. I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the kind of examples you're looking for. Is it okay that my stress is just... regular mom and work stress? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Even if you don’t act on them, do you ever have thoughts that come up that you truly wish would stop because they bother you, even just a little?

Oh, gosh... I feel terrible, I really do, because I know you've asked about this a few different ways now, and I want to be helpful... but no, I really don't. 

I mean, I definitely wish the stress would stop sometimes, you know? Like when there's a mix-up with the doctor's schedules at work and I'm trying to fix it while worrying about what to make for dinner... I wish that overwhelmed feeling would go away. But it's not a specific thought that I want to stop. It's just... the situation, I guess? 

I don't have those kinds of bothersome thoughts that just pop up out of nowhere. My thoughts are all just very focused on what needs to get done. I hope that's alright? I'm trying my best to answer you properly, I promise. I just don't seem to have that particular thing happening.
